traditional_claim: Reduces arthritis pain and body inflammation
scientific_consensus: Curcumin in turmeric has strong anti-inflammatory properties; piperine in black pepper boosts absorption by up to 2000%.
pros: Natural anti-inflammatory; antioxidant-rich; safe in dietary amounts.
cons: Low bioavailability without black pepper; high doses can cause stomach upset or interact with blood thinners.

traditional_claim: Soothes throat irritation and cures viral infections
scientific_consensus: Honey coats the throat and suppresses coughs effectively; lemon provides Vitamin C
pros: though neither cures the underlying virus.
cons: Proven cough suppressant (especially buckwheat honey); keeps you hydrated.
myth_status: Unsafe for infants under 1 year (risk of botulism); high sugar content; lemon acid can erode tooth enamel.

traditional_claim: Melts belly fat rapidly and detoxifies the body
scientific_consensus: Acetic acid can slightly blunt post-meal blood sugar spikes and promote mild fullness
pros: but it does not directly burn fat.
cons: May help manage glycemic response after high-carb meals; inexpensive.
myth_status: Undiluted intake severely damages tooth enamel and esophagus; can lower potassium levels.

myth_status: Clinically proven for pregnancy and chemotherapy-related nausea; anti-inflammatory.
column9: Can cause mild heartburn or diarrhea in large doses; may interact with anticoagulants.

traditional_claim: Lowers blood pressure and prevents common colds
scientific_consensus: Allicin in crushed raw garlic promotes vasodilation (widening of blood vessels)
cons: Supports cardiovascular health; mild antimicrobial properties.
myth_status: Cooking destroys allicin; causes bad breath and body odor; increases bleeding risk before surgery.

traditional_claim: Heals first-degree burns and skin irritation faster
scientific_consensus: Contains glucomannan and gibberellins that stimulate collagen synthesis and skin regeneration.
pros: Cooling relief; speeds up healing for minor superficial burns.
cons: Oral consumption of aloe latex acts as a harsh laxative; rare topical allergic reactions.

traditional_claim: Numbs severe tooth pain and cures cavities
scientific_consensus: Eugenol acts as a natural local anesthetic and antiseptic
cons: though it cannot repair tooth decay.
myth_status: Fast temporary pain relief; strong antibacterial effect against oral bacteria.
column9: Undiluted oil burns gum tissue; toxic if swallowed in large quantities; delays necessary dental care.

traditional_claim: Cools down fresh kitchen burns and prevents blistering
scientific_consensus: Traps heat inside the skin tissue
pros: worsening cellular damage and increasing infection risk.
myth_status: Worsens burn depth; introduces bacteria to damaged skin; makes medical cleaning difficult.

traditional_claim: Relieves headaches when applied to temples and calms stomach cramps
scientific_consensus: Menthol triggers cold-sensitive receptors (TRPM8) to relax muscles and ease tension; enteric-coated capsules relax gut spasms.
pros: Effective topical cooling relief; strong clinical backing for Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS).
cons: Can trigger severe acid reflux (GERD) if taken orally without enteric coating; skin irritation if undiluted.

traditional_claim: Draws out infection and heals swollen throat tissues
scientific_consensus: Creates an osmotic gradient that pulls excess fluid out of swollen tissues
cons: Zero cost; safe; reduces throat swelling and loosens mucus.
myth_status: Does not kill viral infections directly; swallowing large amounts raises sodium intake.

traditional_claim: Draws toxins out of the body overnight through the feet
scientific_consensus: No physiological mechanism exists for onions to pull viruses or toxins through the soles of the feet.
pros: Completely harmless if you enjoy the smell.
cons: Zero medical efficacy; delays proper fever management or hydration.

traditional_claim: Induces deep sleep and calms nervousness
scientific_consensus: Apigenin binds to benzodiazepine receptors in the brain
pros: producing a mild sedative and muscle-relaxing effect.
cons: Gentle relaxation aid; caffeine-free hydration before bed.
myth_status: Can trigger allergic reactions in people sensitive to ragweed or daisies.
